ai.mechanism: Evidence shows only a single transfer of the full USDC balance (balanceRemovedShare 1) out of 0xd3ec0e34aa628c66083759fe35e45ccf73a76d28 on Base. No caller role, permission check, initialisation state, price input or callback trace is supplied, so no exploit mechanism can be named. A sweep by an authorised owner, bridge settlement or migration produces an identical trace.
ai.lossBearer: Unidentified. Nominally the holder(s) of the balance in 0xd3ec0e34aa628c66083759fe35e45ccf73a76d28; the packet names no protocol, no depositor set and no integrators.
ai.narrative: A contract on Base was emptied of its entire USDC balance in one transaction: 789,437.589058 USDC, about $789,438. That is the whole story the data tells. There is no protocol label, no attacker attribution, no sign of a broken access check, no stale oracle print and no reentrant call. A treasury moving its own funds, a bridge settling, or a migration would look exactly like this. The exposure record lists zero integrators, so no downstream counterparty loss is demonstrated. Until something identifies the mover as unauthorised, this is a large transfer, not a proven exploit, and there is no evidenced loss path to trade against.
